title: Black-and-White Cookies
summary: Large, soft cake-like cookies iced in a neat split of vanilla and chocolate icing, a classic New York bakery treat.
equipment: 2 large metal baking trays lined with baking paper
stand mixer or electric hand whisk
60 ml (1/4 cup-size) scoop or large spoon
offset spatula or small palette knife

ingredients.item: fine sea salt or table salt, or table salt

ingredients.note: plus a little more if needed

steps.title: Heat the oven
steps.text: Heat the oven to 190°C (170°C fan) for at least 20 minutes before baking. These cake-like cookies need a properly hot oven from the start to set their shape before spreading too far.

steps.title: Cream butter and sugar
steps.text: Beat the butter and caster sugar on medium speed for 3-4 minutes until light, then beat in the eggs one at a time, followed by the vanilla and lemon zest. Beating the butter and sugar well here builds the air that keeps these cookies soft and cake-like rather than dense.

steps.title: Mix wet and dry separately
steps.text: Whisk the flour, baking powder, bicarbonate of soda and salt together in one bowl, and mix the soured cream with the milk in another. Keeping them separate until needed means they combine evenly once added.

steps.title: Combine in stages
steps.text: Add the dry and wet mixtures alternately to the creamed butter, in three additions of dry and two of wet, mixing on low until you have a thick, cake-like batter. Alternating this way stops the batter curdling or turning lumpy.

steps.title: Scoop and bake
steps.text: Scoop 60g mounds of batter 7cm apart, six per tray, and flatten each slightly with a wet spoon. Bake one tray at a time for 11-14 minutes, until the tops spring back when pressed and the edges are just turning golden.

steps.title: Cool completely
steps.text: Cool on the tray for 5 minutes, then move to a wire rack to cool completely. The icing won't set properly on a warm cookie, so don't rush this step.

steps.title: Make the icing
steps.text: Whisk the icing sugar, golden syrup, vanilla and boiling water together to a thick, smooth, spreadable glaze, adding a little more water if needed. The golden syrup helps keep the icing glossy and stops it setting too brittle.

steps.title: Ice the halves
steps.text: Turn the cooled cookies flat-side up and spread the plain vanilla icing over half of each one. Icing the flat underside, as is traditional, gives a smoother finish than the domed top.

steps.title: Make and apply the chocolate icing
steps.text: Stir the melted chocolate and cocoa powder into the remaining icing, loosening with a few drops of hot water if it's too thick, then spread over the other half of each cookie. Set aside for 1 hour until the icing is firm to the touch before serving.

tips: Let the cookies cool completely before icing - a common mistake is icing them while still warm, which melts the icing straight off instead of letting it set in a neat line.
Measure the dough into even 60g mounds so every cookie bakes through at the same rate.
Ice the flat underside of the cookie rather than the domed top, which gives a much neater, flatter surface for the split pattern.
Keep the dividing line between the two icings reasonably straight by icing one half first and letting it firm up slightly before adding the other.
If the chocolate icing seizes or thickens too fast, loosen it with a few drops of hot water rather than adding more melted chocolate.
Don't taste the raw dough or batter: raw flour and raw egg aren't safe to eat until baked.
storage: Store in an airtight container at room temperature for up to 3 days, as the soft icing can soften further in the fridge. They don't freeze well once iced, though the plain baked cookies can be frozen for up to 1 month and iced after thawing.
